title: Halden Grocers: closing the margin gap

cover.title: Halden Grocers: closing the margin gap to the regional leaders
cover.sub: Three operating moves that lift EBITDA margin from {m_now} to {m_target} within three years.

exec.title: Halden can lift margin by {m_gap} in three years without closing a single store

rows.p: Sales reached {sales} across {stores} stores, and customer scores lead the region for the fourth year running. Like-for-like sales grew in every quarter, and the store estate needs no major refit before the plan period ends.

EBITDA margin of {m_now2} sits {gap_lead} behind the best regional peer, mostly in fresh shrink and store labour. Cost inflation in both lines is running ahead of what Halden can pass on to customers.
Fresh supply rebuild, labour scheduling and own-label range. Together they add {uplift} of EBITDA at today's sales, with each move owned by one executive and tracked monthly by the board.

chart.title: Halden sits fourth of six regional grocers on margin, behind every scaled peer

bullets: The three leaders all run central fresh buying; Halden buys fresh store by store.
Shrink alone explains about {shrink_pp} of the gap to the leader.
Halden is ahead of the two smaller chains on every cost line.
takeaway.sowhat: The gap is operational, not structural: the leaders show it can be closed.

chart.source: Source: annual reports of the six grocers (all fictional); specimen team analysis
chart.note: Margins on a pre-IFRS 16 basis for comparability.
